Text: Sleek river folk who would rather swim than walk, Otters farm, filter and dig the water from day one. On land they are slow, and they tire once their fur dries out. Their motto: Clean water, warm dens, and a good swim.
The rivers ran dry, and your Otters with them. This is the end.
Congratulations! You mastered the Otters' water-bound ways and used this map's rivers to build the faction's wonder.
The rivers run clean again, and every one of them leads home.
Dry fur. Works slower until it gets wet again.
"Why blow it up when you can just dig?" —Old Eddy
Cleans badwater at its intake through a bundle of reeds. Works faster the dirtier the water. Keeps working when flooded.
"The reeds don't mind the taste. I asked." —Nan Rillwhisker
A clean-water soak that washes badwater contamination out of otters.
In through the badwater, out through the rinse.
Digs out the terrain underneath it by paw, leaving a little dirt behind.
A den out in the water. Residents' fur dries out slower while they sleep. Must stand in water. Keeps working when flooded.
A bigger holt that fits more otters. Must stand in water. Keeps working when flooded.
Grows with its feet in the water and its head in the sun.
Big leaves above, starchy roots below.
Employs a fisher who catches fish in the water below. Badwater scares the fish away. Keeps working when flooded.
"Patience, a long rod, and a longer lunch." —Old Eddy
A log-framed swimming hole in the river. Soaks otters' fur. Keeps working when flooded.
Last one in is a dry beaver.
Brings up clean water from deep underground, even in droughts and badtides, and pours it out of its back or into <YellowHighlight>Water Tubes</YellowHighlight>. Breaks down from time to time.
Deep down, the river never ends.
The water has nowhere to go.
Well water has nowhere to go
Carries water from an Artesian Well to Tube Outlets.
Pours out the water brought by Water Tubes.
Where the river comes back out.
A slide tower with a chute into the river. Soaks otters' fur. Keeps working when flooded.
A mud ramp for slipping into the river. Place it against a riverbank.
A Water Tube that can be closed. Pause it to stop the water.
Every outlet on this well's line is closed.
Employs a gatherer who raises clams on a clean, shallow riverbed. Keeps working when flooded.
Happy as a clam, as long as the water's clean.
Needs shallow, clean water over the bed.
Catches driftwood from flowing water. Works faster in a stronger current. Keeps working when flooded.
"Somebody upstream is very bad at keeping track of their logs." —Old Eddy
A sunny spot where otters doze on warm stones. Keeps working when flooded.
Wet fur, warm stone, no plans.
A fast, if drafty, means of otter transportation.
A fast, if drafty, means of otter transportation. Connects upward.
Up the ladder, down the slide.
A fast, watertight means of otter transportation. Blocks off water.
For once, the otters want to stay dry.
A Timber Tunnel network entrance and exit.
Mind the gap. And the tail.
The Otters' wonder: a great log fountain that lifts the river high above the town.
Every river starts somewhere. This one starts here.
